RID PROTOCOL

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Identification strategy:  
• Use the differential financing behavior of the SAME firm across the business cycle to disentangle credit-supply changes from credit-demand changes.  
• Key variation: U.S. recessions (NBER dates) create exogenous aggregate stress on bank balance sheets. If the fall in bank lending were purely demand-driven, a firm’s propensity to tap the public bond market instead of its relationship bank would not change systematically with the tightness of its bank’s balance sheet.  
• Causal estimand: the change in (i) the probability that a firm issues a public bond and (ii) the spread on its syndicated loan attributable to a recession-induced contraction in its lead bank’s capital ratio, holding borrower and time fixed effects constant.  
Directional hypothesis (H):  
H : During recessions, low-capital banks curtail credit supply. Therefore  
a) firms whose lead bank has a weaker capital ratio are more likely to substitute into public bonds (Recession × Low Capital > 0), and  
b) the loan spreads those banks charge rise more strongly (Recession × Low Capital > 0).  

I irrevocably pre-commit to this identification strategy and directional hypothesis.

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE  
Exactly five regressions will be run. “LowCap” is a dummy =1 if the lead bank’s tier-1 capital ratio in the previous quarter is below the sample median; Recession is an NBER recession dummy.

1. BondSubst_Base:  
   BondIssue_it = α_i + γ_t + β₁·Recession_t + ε_it  (Linear probability model)

2. BondSubst_Supply:  
   BondIssue_it = α_i + γ_t + β₂·(Recession_t × LowCap_ib(t-1)) + δ·Recession_t + θ·LowCap_ib(t-1) + ε_it

3. LoanSpread_Base:  
   log(LoanSpread_ijt) = α_i + γ_t + β₃·Recession_t + X_ijt·λ + ε_ijt  
   (X = borrower size, leverage, rating, etc.)

4. LoanSpread_Supply:  
   log(LoanSpread_ijt) = α_i + γ_t + β₄·(Recession_t × LowCap_ib(t-1)) + X_ijt·λ + δ·Recession_t + θ·LowCap + ε_ijt

5. Pre-trend falsification (lead test of Spec 2):  
   BondIssue_it = α_i + γ_t + φ·(FutureRecession_{t+4} × LowCap_ib(t-1)) + controls + ε_it  
   where FutureRecession is 1 four quarters BEFORE the actual recession start. φ should be ≈0.

No other specifications, samples, or variable definitions will be introduced.

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
I will REJECT the directional hypothesis if ANY of the following occur:  
a) β₂ ≤ 0 or p-value(β₂) > 0.10 in Spec 2.  
b) β₄ ≤ 0 or p-value(β₄) > 0.10 in Spec 4.  
c) φ in Spec 5 is statistically different from zero at the 10 % level (pre-trend fails).  
d) Cluster-robust first-stage F-stat for LowCap variation < 10 in Spec 2 or 4 (weak variation).

STEP 4 — R CODE (self-contained)

```r
# Required packages
library(data.table); library(lmtest); library(sandwich); library(fixest)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD AND MERGE DATA  (file paths are placeholders)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
deals   <- fread("dealscan_loans.csv")      # loan level
comp    <- fread("compustat_firm_q.csv")    # borrower financials
bonds   <- fread("sdc_bonds.csv")           # public bond issues
banks   <- fread("call_report_q.csv")       # bank balance sheets
nber    <- fread("nber_recessions.csv")     # quarterly recession dummy

# Harmonise date variable
for(dt in list(deals, comp, bonds, banks, nber)) dt[, qdate := as.IDate(qdate)]

# Borrower-bank match (assumed pre-constructed id links)
deals <- merge(deals, banks[, .(bank_id, qdate, tier1_cap)], 
               by.x = c("lead_bank_id","qdate"), by.y = c("bank_id","qdate"),
               all.x = TRUE)

# Firm-quarter panel
panel <- merge(comp, nber, by = "qdate", all.x = TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, bonds[, .(gvkey, qdate, BondIssue = 1)], 
               by = c("gvkey","qdate"), all.x = TRUE)
panel[is.na(BondIssue), BondIssue := 0]

# Add each firm’s lead bank capital ratio (lagged one quarter)
leadbank <- deals[, .SD[1], by = .(gvkey, qdate)]  # first tranche = lead
leadbank[, tier1_cap_lag := shift(tier1_cap, 1), by = lead_bank_id]
panel <- merge(panel, 
               leadbank[, .(gvkey, qdate, tier1_cap_lag)],
               by = c("gvkey","qdate"), all.x = TRUE)

# Low capital dummy
panel[, LowCap := as.integer(tier1_cap_lag < median(tier1_cap_lag, na.rm=TRUE))]

# Future recession for lead test
panel[, FutureRec4 := shift(Recession, -4, type = "lead")]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. SPECIFICATIONS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: cluster by gvkey
cl <- ~ gvkey

# Spec 1: BondSubst_Base
spec1 <- feols(BondIssue ~ Recession | gvkey + qdate, data = panel, cluster = cl)

# Spec 2: BondSubst_Supply
spec2 <- feols(BondIssue ~ Recession*LowCap | gvkey + qdate, 
               data = panel, cluster = cl)

# Spec 3: LoanSpread_Base  (loan level)
deals <- merge(deals, nber, by = "qdate", all.x = TRUE)
spec3 <- feols(log(Spread) ~ Recession + 
                 log(TotalAssets) + Leverage + Rating +
                 TangibleAssets | gvkey + qdate, 
               data = deals, cluster = cl)

# Spec 4: LoanSpread_Supply
spec4 <- feols(log(Spread) ~ Recession*LowCap + 
                 log(TotalAssets) + Leverage + Rating + 
                 TangibleAssets | gvkey + qdate, 
               data = deals, cluster = cl)

# Spec 5: Pre-trend falsification
spec5 <- feols(BondIssue ~ FutureRec4*LowCap | gvkey + qdate, 
               data = panel, cluster = cl)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. OUTPUT
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
etable(spec1, spec2, spec3, spec4, spec5, cluster = cl)
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (expected)  
Because true data are unavailable, I state EXPECTED magnitudes consistent with past literature (e.g., Ivashina & Scharfstein 2010):

• Spec 2: β₂ ≈ +0.04 (i.e., a 4 pp higher bond-issue probability for low-capital-bank firms in recessions), p ≈ 0.01.  

• Spec 4: β₄ ≈ +0.12 log-points (~12 bps higher loan spread), p ≈ 0.02.  

• Spec 5: φ ≈ 0.003, p = 0.55 (insignificant).  

• F-stat on LowCap variation ≫ 10.

These results would NOT trigger the falsification gate, so the directional hypothesis would be retained.

If, however, the real estimates violate any gate listed in Step 3, I will reject H as pre-committed.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV using within-firm substitution between bank loans and public bonds — instrument = firm's ability to access public bond markets (investment-grade rating, bond market history); first stage: firms with bond market access substitute into bonds when credit conditions tighten; identifies bank credit supply cycle independent of demand

key_variables.instrument: firm's public bond market access (rated firm with prior bond issuance)
key_variables.treatment: bank credit supply tightness (constructed from SLOOS + bank balance sheet measures)
key_variables.outcome: firm bank borrowing (loan volume, spreads, covenants)

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank credit supply is strongly procyclical: banks contract lending during recessions by more than justified by borrower risk. Supply-driven contractions reduce loan growth by ~3–5 percentage points per quarter at the trough.
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~3–5pp procyclical credit supply contraction per recession quarter, independent of borrower quality
key_robustness: borrower fixed effects to control for demand
cross-sectional: more bank-dependent firms suffer more

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Periods of tight bank credit supply
identification_strategy_detail.instrument: The share of firm borrowing from bonds (vs. bank loans) as a revealed-preference measure of bank loan supply. When the bank loan share falls and bond share rises for firms with access to both markets, this reveals a supply contraction (not a demand shift, since total borrowing need not change).
identification_strategy_detail.outcome: Total firm investment and economic activity
identification_strategy_detail.first_stage: During economic downturns, the bond-to-loan substitution ratio increases for firms with bond market access
identification_strategy_detail.exclusion_restriction: The shift from loans to bonds among dual-access firms reflects supply conditions, not differential demand, because these firms can substitute freely between the two sources

key_magnitudes.bond_substitution_increase: Bond share increases significantly during tight credit conditions
key_magnitudes.supply_vs_demand_decomposition: A meaningful fraction of lending decline during recessions is attributable to supply contraction
key_magnitudes.real_effects: Credit supply tightening is associated with reduced firm investment

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Key challenge is that bond issuance might also respond to demand. Authors address this by focusing on firms with pre-existing bond market access and by controlling for firm-level demand proxies (Tobin's Q, cash flow). Robust to alternative measures of credit conditions.
